title: The ballroom donor list in full: who gave, what they had pending
summary: The October 2025 roster of about 37 donors is documented. The amounts come from a single leaked spreadsheet relayed by the Washington Post (67 donations, about $333M, at least $77M anonymous), which Reuters did not verify. Many donors had a significant federal matter within six months of the list date. The tightest documented pairings are Rocket (FHFA approval three weeks before a $10M pledge), Herrera ($2.5M four months before her father's pardon), Ergen (FCC probe closed before, spectrum approval after), the Winklevoss twins (CFTC nominee withdrawn three weeks before the list) and Paxos (OCC charter 50 days after). Every link from gift to decision is inferred. Gift dates are mostly unknown, and the counter-cases (Booz Allen, Comcast, Union Pacific, Meta, Google, Amazon) and batch or generic decisions cut against a systematic pay-for-favour reading.

sub_claims.statement: The two lists: the White House's October 2025 roster (about 37 names, no amounts) and the Washington Post's leaked spreadsheet (October 2026: 67 donations above $10,000, about $333M).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented for the October 2025 list (White House release relayed by AP, CNBC, Fortune, Spectrum/NBC). The White House named donors on 2025-10-23, after a 2025-10-15 East Room dinner, gave no amounts and said the list was incomplete. Outlets count 36 or 37 names (21 corporations plus 15-16 individuals or family foundations). Single-source for the spreadsheet: the Post published it on 2026-10-15, and other outlets relay it. It records 67 donations above $10,000 totalling about $333M as of late September 2026, at least $77M of it from donors who asked for anonymity. It excludes in-kind gifts and does not list Trump. Reuters said it had not verified the document. The White House called the conflict concerns 'fake' and vowed to find the leaker. The Post itself says its reporting does not show that any donation led to a government action. Audit: the 67 donations / ~$333M / at least $77M anonymous figures are confirmed across several relays (IBTimes, Mediaite, NPR affiliates WYPR/KJZZ). One NPR-affiliate transcript speaks of about 57 major donors, so donor counts vary by outlet.

sub_claims.statement: Top tier ($25M each): Apple, Nvidia, the Adelson Family Foundation and Charles Ergen.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source (WaPo spreadsheet, relayed by MacRumors, 9to5Mac, the Boston Globe, Casino.org and TNW). Apple and Nvidia are each at $25M, and Nvidia asked to stay anonymous; it was absent from the 2025 list. The Adelson Family Foundation (Miriam Adelson) is at $25M. Ergen's $25M came as $12.5M in December 2025, anonymous at his request, and $12.5M in February 2026. One early summary refers to an unidentified 'third $25M donor' and an unidentified $12.5M donor, which conflicts with the four $25M names other outlets report. We could not resolve this without the Post's article. Gift dates are public only for Ergen (Dec 2025 and Feb 2026) and Nvidia (Oct 2025, per the Post).

sub_claims.statement: Apple ($25M): the Aug 2025 chip-tariff exemption and the DOJ antitrust case.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented matters; any link is inferred. On 2025-08-06 Trump announced a roughly 100% tariff on imported chips, exempting companies that build in the US, and named Apple as exempt. That came after Apple raised its US investment pledge to $600B, a figure analysts said includes ordinary spending. The DOJ's 2024 iPhone monopoly suit survived Apple's motion to dismiss in June 2025. Bloomberg reported early settlement talks in July 2026, with Apple making several offers; no settlement has been announced. Timing: Apple's gift date is not public. Apple was on the 23 Oct 2025 list, about 11 weeks after the exemption, which is within six months, but we cannot tell whether the gift came before or after it. What cuts against a favour reading: the exemption was a general rule tied to an investment pledge, and other investors got it too. No source links it to the ballroom.

sub_claims.statement: Charles Ergen/EchoStar ($25M): the FCC closed its EchoStar probe on 2025-09-08, three months before his first anonymous $12.5M. It approved the $40B AT&T and SpaceX spectrum sales on 2026-05-12, about three months after his second $12.5M.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented FCC actions (Satellite Today, Fierce, Advanced Television); gift dates single-source (WaPo); the link is inferred. Carr's 8 Sep 2025 letter told staff to wrap up the 5G buildout probe hours after EchoStar agreed to sell spectrum to SpaceX for about $17B, a couple of weeks after a roughly $23B sale to AT&T. Both later actions fall within six months of a tranche. Cuts against: the probe closed before any gift, so the sequence fits gratitude at most, not an exchange, and that too is unsourced. The May 2026 approval imposed a $2.4B escrow condition that EchoStar protested (C69). Ergen's anonymity request for the first tranche is documented in the leak. This extends C69, which dated only the 2026 order. Audit: Ergen's two $12.5M tranches (Dec 2025, anonymous at his request; Feb 2026) are confirmed in the leak coverage; Ergen and EchoStar declined to comment.

sub_claims.statement: Rocket Companies (a subsidiary, $10M): the pledge came about three weeks after the FHFA approved Rocket's $9.4B Mr. Cooper takeover (2025-08-26). Rocket was not on the public list.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented approval (HousingWire, MPA); single-source gift and timing (the Post, relayed by IBTimes and Alternet). This is the one pairing the Post itself sets out, and it says the record does not show causation. The FHFA, led by Bill Pulte, cleared the deal with 20% concentration caps at Fannie and Freddie, which cuts slightly against a pure favour reading. An earlier layer is just outside six months: the CFPB dismissed its kickback suit against Rocket Homes with prejudice on 2025-02-27, about 6.5 months before the gift. The gift is among the roughly 30 donations kept off the October 2025 list. Audit: the FHFA approval (26-27 Aug 2025, 20% caps) is confirmed by the FHFA's own release and trade press. Two fresh searches did not surface the $10M Rocket pledge outside the outlets already cited, so the gift and its timing were not independently re-confirmed and remain single-source (the Post via IBTimes/Alternet).

sub_claims.statement: Isabela Herrera ($2.5M, Sep 2025): her father, banker Julio Herrera Velutini, was pardoned on 2026-01-15, about four months later.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented pardon (Bloomberg Law, DOJ filing reported by NOTUS); single-source gift (WaPo via secondary outlets); the link is inferred. Separately, she gave MAGA Inc. about $3.5M, and her company hired Alina Habba on a reported deal worth more than $50M over four years. Habba says she had no role in the pardon. A White House official denied that the donations played any part. The pardon also covered ex-governor Wanda Vazquez and Mark Rossini, and the case had already been cut to a misdemeanour plea in August 2025. The Post does not establish a link. Former pardon attorney Liz Oyer called the ballroom a 'money laundering operation', which is opinion. Audit: confirmed via Telemundo/EFE and Primera Hora. Her MAGA Inc. gifts were $2.5M on 31 Dec 2024, while her father faced bribery charges, and $1M in late July 2025, after the most serious charges were dropped. The ballroom pledge came about two months after the second gift. The Campaign Legal Center has filed an FEC complaint alleging Herrera Velutini, a Venezuelan national, may have funded the contributions through his daughter (an allegation). The Habba contract figure varies: '>$50M over four years' (Law Commentary) vs. '$40M' in a secondary summary of NYT reporting.

sub_claims.statement: The Loeffler-Sprecher fund ($5M): a sitting cabinet official's household gave. Her husband's ICE invested up to $2B in Polymarket on 2025-10-07, a company in which Donald Trump Jr. and 1789 Capital have stakes.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source gift (WaPo, relayed by the Daily Beast and Engadget); the ICE-Polymarket deal is documented (AJC, Blockworks), as are Don Jr.'s stake and adviser role (C25). The chain from the ballroom gift to Polymarket to the Trump family is inferred: no outlet we found links them. Kelly Loeffler heads the SBA, and Jeff Sprecher chairs Intercontinental Exchange, the NYSE's owner. DOJ and the CFTC closed their Polymarket probes on 2025-07-15, before both the ICE deal and the October list, so this was not relief bought with the gift. The gift date is not public.

sub_claims.statement: The Winklevoss twins (listed separately in Oct 2025): the White House withdrew Brian Quintenz's CFTC nomination on 2025-09-30, about three weeks before the list, after the twins lobbied against him.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented withdrawal and lobbying (Decrypt, NOTUS, Bloomberg Government). Quintenz released Tyler Winklevoss's texts arguing that the CFTC had treated Gemini unfairly; Gemini calls the account false. The White House gave no reason, and reports also cite Senate holds and Quintenz's Kalshi ties. Amounts: we found no figure from the leak for the twins. A crypto outlet's '$5.1M from the Winklevoss twins' appears to be a political-giving tally, not a ballroom gift, and is unverified. Linking the withdrawal to the ballroom gift is our own inference. C52 covers the texts; what is new here is the dating against the list.

sub_claims.statement: Charles and Marissa Cascarilla (Paxos CEO), listed in Oct 2025: the OCC approved Paxos's national trust charter conversion on 2025-12-12, 50 days after the list.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented approval (Paxos release, Blockworks); listing documented (2025 roster as relayed by Spectrum/NBC); the link is inferred. Paxos filed in August 2025. The same-day batch included Ripple, another donor, as well as Circle, BitGo and Fidelity Digital Assets, which are not on the list (C69). The batch is an innocent explanation, and the gift date is unknown. Previous reports noted Ripple's charter but not that Paxos's CEO was also a named donor.

sub_claims.statement: Tether America (Oct 2025 list): it hired former White House crypto council director Bo Hines in Sept 2025 and launched USAT on 2026-01-27 through federally chartered Anchorage, with Lutnick's former firm Cantor as reserve custodian.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (The Block). No federal approval to Tether itself was found. USAT is issued by Anchorage Digital Bank under the GENIUS Act framework (C11). The Cantor and Lutnick links are in C35 and C50, and Tether is a Miller Strategies client (C64). No amount was found in the leak coverage we could reach. This is a revolving-door and structural link, not a dated favour.

sub_claims.statement: T-Mobile ($5M): the FCC approved its $4.4B UScellular deal and its Metronet JV in July 2025, after T-Mobile told Chair Carr it was ending DEI programmes.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented approval and DEI letter (Insurance Journal/Reuters, PhoneArena); single-source amount (WaPo, as relayed in leak coverage; we could not confirm which outlet first reported the T-Mobile figure); the link is inferred. The approval came about three months before the list. Commissioner Gomez called the DEI move a 'cynical bid to win FCC regulatory approval'. The FCC did not tie its decision to DEI. DOJ had already cleared the deal.

sub_claims.statement: Micron (Oct 2025 list): Commerce renegotiated its $6.1B CHIPS award and added $275M on 2025-06-12, alongside a $200B investment pledge.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (Commerce release, MeriTalk); the link is inferred. The award came about four months before the list. Cuts against: it was a renegotiation Trump ordered for all Biden-era CHIPS deals, and it came with a larger company commitment. No amount was found.

sub_claims.statement: Altria and Reynolds American (Oct 2025 list): the White House withdrew the menthol ban on 2025-01-21, and the FDA authorized Altria's on! PLUS pouches in late Dec 2025.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented (Reuters, C-Store Dive); the link is inferred. The menthol withdrawal is about nine months before the list, outside the window, and predates the ballroom announcement. The on! PLUS authorization (about two months after the list) was the first decision under an FDA pilot programme. Public Citizen's table shows no pending federal enforcement against Altria. No amounts were found.

sub_claims.statement: Counter-cases: donors that received adverse federal action within six months (Booz Allen, Comcast, Union Pacific, Meta, Google, Amazon, AT&T).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented. Booz Allen: Treasury cancelled all 31 of its contracts (about $21M) on 2026-01-26 over the Littlejohn tax leak, and AP framed it as retribution 'despite' the ballroom gift. Comcast: FCC DEI probe (Feb 2025), then an affiliate probe in July 2025 days after a Trump post. Union Pacific: the STB rejected its Norfolk Southern merger filing as incomplete on 2026-01-16, then accepted a refiling on 2026-05-28. Meta: lost the FTC case only in court (2025-11-18), and the FTC appealed (C33). Google: DOJ cross-appealed for a Chrome divestiture (Feb 2026); its $22M is a settlement, not a gift (C33). Amazon: $2.5B FTC penalty on 2025-09-25 (C69). AT&T: listed at $5M 'pledged', which AT&T denies; it was a buyer in the FCC-approved EchoStar deal. These cut against a simple pay-for-favour reading of the whole list.

sub_claims.statement: Donors who were already appointees: Ambassadors Joseph Popolo Jr. ($1M, Netherlands) and Benjamin Leon Jr. (listed, Spain), and SBA Administrator Loeffler.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: documented appointments (Local10, Florida Politics, NL Times, DutchNews); Popolo's amount single-source (WaPo). Timing cuts against an appointment-for-gift reading: both ambassadors were named in early January 2025, months before the ballroom was announced in mid-2025. The Post says it does not suggest Popolo got his post because of the gift. Separately, Konstantin Sokolov, a listed donor, was named in July 2026 to chair the State Department's $201M Tripp+ fund (C70). That is about nine months after the list, outside six months of the list date, but his gift date is unknown.

sub_claims.statement: Brandon Lutnick ($2.5M) and the Lutnick Family listing.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source and weak. One search-result summary of the leak coverage gives Brandon Lutnick $2.5M, and a second search could not confirm it. 'The Lutnick Family' is on the 2025 list (documented). His father, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, oversees export licences, CHIPS awards and tariff exemptions that bear on other donors on this list (Apple, Micron, Nvidia). The Lutnick sons now run Cantor (C35). This is a structural conflict and no specific matter is dated.

sub_claims.statement: Already in C68/C69, not repeated here: Nvidia (Oct 2025 gift; UAE/Saudi licences 2025-11-19; H200 China 2025-12-08), Microsoft ($10M; UAE licences Sep 2025), Palantir ($10M; Navy ShipOS 2025-12-09), Lockheed ($10M; F-35 Lot 18-19 2025-09-29), Ripple (charter 2025-12-12).
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: amounts single-source (WaPo); acts documented; links inferred. See C68 and C69 for findings and innocent explanations (the Lockheed deal was agreed in Nov 2024; the charters came in a batch).

sub_claims.statement: Advocacy-group aggregates: Public Citizen counts most corporate donors as federal contractors or as facing enforcement.
sub_claims.finding: Evidence grade: single-source (advocacy). Nov 2025: 14 of 24 corporate donors faced federal enforcement or had it suspended, and the donors held $279B in contracts over five years. June 2026: 14 of 27 got new or increased contracts, about $50B in six months. We did not reconcile these figures with USASpending. Reuters (Apr 2026) reports the Trust for the National Mall contract lets donors stay anonymous and has limited conflict safeguards.

corrections: The claim's 'Ergen $25M' is right but was given in two $12.5M tranches (Dec 2025, anonymous; Feb 2026), per the Post.
Google's $22M is the YouTube settlement routed to the ballroom (C33), not a voluntary gift.
AT&T's $5M is marked 'pledged' in the spreadsheet, and AT&T denies giving or planning to give.
The leaked figures were current as of late September 2026 and exclude in-kind gifts (e.g. Carrier's offered HVAC system). Reuters did not verify the document.

The 2026-10-15 date on leaked amounts is the publication date, not the gift date. Only Nvidia (Oct 2025), Ergen (Dec 2025 and Feb 2026), Herrera (Sep 2025) and Rocket (about mid-Sep 2025) have gift timing in the coverage we found.

Crypto donors' amounts (Coinbase, Ripple, Tether, Winklevoss) were not found in the leak coverage we could reach. A '$5M each' figure in crypto media appears to describe political spending and is unverified as ballroom giving.
denials_and_context: The White House called the leak-based conflict claims 'fake' and said it would pursue the leaker. A White House official denied that the Herrera donations played any role in the pardon.
The Washington Post says its reporting does not show that any donation led to a government action, and does not suggest Popolo's ambassadorship resulted from his gift.
Nvidia says its support was independent of business interests (C68). AT&T denies giving. Habba denies any role in the Herrera pardon. Gemini disputes Quintenz's account of the texts.

Gift dates are mostly unknown: only the 2025-10-23 list date and the 2026-10-15 leak date are public for most donors, so most six-month windows are measured from the list date, and a gift could sit on either side of an official act.

Several official acts were general rules or batch decisions (the chip-tariff exemption for US investors, the five-charter OCC batch, Trump's order to renegotiate all CHIPS awards), and several donors received adverse treatment (Booz Allen, Comcast, Union Pacific, Meta, Google, Amazon).
Ergen and EchoStar declined to comment on his gift. The Campaign Legal Center's FEC complaint about the Herrera MAGA Inc. contributions is an allegation, not a finding.

leads.title: The ~30 donors the White House kept off its October 2025 list
leads.why_connected: The spreadsheet has 67 donations against 37 public names, with at least $77M anonymous. Only a few of the hidden donors (Nvidia, Rocket, Ergen's first tranche, Herrera, Popolo, Loeffler-Sprecher, Cisco, ServiceNow, AT&T) were identified in the coverage we could reach. The rest need a row-by-row pass over the Post's article.

leads.title: Rocket Companies: CFPB dismissal, FHFA approval, then a $10M ballroom pledge
leads.why_connected: Three dated events in seven months involving one company and two agencies whose heads were Trump appointees (Pulte at FHFA). No report in this project covers Rocket.

leads.title: Herrera family: ballroom, MAGA Inc., Habba retainer and the Jan 2026 pardon
leads.why_connected: Daughter's $2.5M ballroom gift and $3.5M super-PAC gifts, the Habba retainer, and the father's pardon. Belongs with C36/C49 pardon research.

leads.title: Loeffler-Sprecher: a cabinet official's ballroom gift and ICE's Polymarket stake
leads.why_connected: An SBA Administrator's household gift, with her husband's exchange co-investing alongside Don Jr.'s 1789 Capital in Polymarket. Worth checking against OGE ethics agreements and CFTC actions on Polymarket after Oct 2025.

leads.title: AT&T denies its $5M 'pledged' entry
leads.why_connected: The only 'pledged' row; AT&T was a buyer in the FCC-approved EchoStar deal. The discrepancy tests the spreadsheet's reliability.
